newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: S.Korea asks Cambodia to investigate shooting.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea asks Cambodia to investigate shooting.

text.p: South Korea asked the Cambodian government on Thursday to conduct a thorough investigation into the shooting and wounding of a Korean national, diplomats said.

An unidentified gunman on Tuesday night shot Kim Sang-yul as he was driving in his car in the capital, police and South Korean diplomats said, adding that he was under intensive care at Phnom Penh's Calmette Hospital.

"The ambassador (Park Kyung-tai) went to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to demand a thorough investigation," said a South Korean diplomat, whose country opened low-level ties with Cambodia this year after a 21-year hiatus.
The results of the meeting were not known, but the diplomat said the ambassador was expected to decide later in the day whether Kim should be sent back to South Korea for treatment.
City police chief Mok Chito said Kim was hit once under the right armpit.
"I don't think this was a murder or robbery attempt," he said. "Maybe it was sudden anger after an argument in a restaurant. I don't think it's politically motivated."
The police chief said Kim, 45, was the former manager of the Plaza hotel but was now in other business.
Interior Ministry spokesman Sok Phal said he was worried that the shooting could give Cambodia a poor image overseas.
The capital was hit by a wave of crimes against foreigners earlier this year, including the rape of a French woman and the shooting wounding of a French man.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who visited Seoul in July, has trumpeted the renewed ties between the two countries and has encouraged South Korean businessmen to invest Cambodia.
